Bug_Details:
In Java, the Object.equals() method is used for object comparison, and it is typically overridden in classes to provide a custom
equality check based on your criteria for equality.
The default implementation of equals() provided by the Object class compares the memory references of the two objects,
that means it checks if the objects are actually the same instance in memory.
The "equals" as a method name should be used exclusively to override Object.equals(Object) to prevent confusion.
It is important to note that when you override equals() , you should also override the hashCode() method to maintain the
contract between equals() and hashCode() .
Bug_Explanation: The CustomPoint class incorrectly overrides the equals method by taking a parameter of type CustomPoint instead of Object. This violates the contract of the equals method in the Object class, which should take an Object parameter. This means that when equals is called with an Object, the method from Object is invoked instead of the intended logic.
Trigger_Explanation: The test cases use the 'showBug' method, which in turn uses the incorrect 'equals' method. This method accepts a parameter of type CustomPoint instead of Object, violating the contract of the equals method in the Object class. As a result, the test cases that compare CustomPoint objects using the equals method fail when the parameter type is Object, triggering the bug.
